title: Working Zones Introduction and Seal Ring's Housing
topics: Seal ring housing working zones introduction
Bearing and seal ring assembly with same fitting diameter
rules: Working zone introduction for seal rings in housing must include lead-in chamfer with angle 15° ± 5° and depth proportional to diameter
Chamfer radius R depends on diameter: ød ≤ 60 use R=0.4, >60 to ≤120 use R=0.8, >120 use R=1.2
Minimum effective dimension a = 1 mm (effective minimum) unless larger dimensioning is not permitted, constrained to a ≤ 2 mm
For bearing and seal ring with same fitting diameter (dc = da): seal ring assembly must follow bearing assembly
All zone 'L' dimensions must be equal when bearing and seal ring share fitting diameter
Specific zones must remain the same and useful length assigned
Rounded edge indication means there must be no sharp roughness
Surface possibly with plunge grinding machining and without roughness a/o helical ridges
dimensions: Chamfer radius R: 0.4 mm for ød ≤ 60
Chamfer radius R: 0.8 mm for 60 < ød ≤ 120
Chamfer radius R: 1.2 mm for ød > 120
tolerances: Fitting tolerance and roughness values must be indicated in technical zones
surface_finish: Surface possibly with plunge grinding machining
No sharp edges or roughness allowed on rounded edges
Roughness values must be specified in technical zones
inspection: Verify effective dimension a is minimum 1 mm and maximum 2 mm
Verify appropriate radius R based on diameter range
Verify rounded edges have no sharp roughness
Check surface for absence of helical ridges
manufacturing_notes: Spigot rounded or rounded side must have sharp edge removed
Use plunge grinding for surface finish where applicable
Ensure no helical ridges remain after machining
When assembling bearing and seal ring with same diameter: seal ring follows bearing in sequence
All technical zones must indicate fitting tolerance and roughness values
training_guidance: NX agent should create seal ring housing pockets with 15° ± 5° lead-in chamfer
Apply diameter-dependent fillet radius: R=0.4 for small (≤60mm), R=0.8 for medium (60-120mm), R=1.2 for large (>120mm) seal seats
Maintain effective working dimension 'a' between 1-2 mm on housing seal pockets
When modeling combined bearing-seal assemblies with shared fitting diameter, ensure zone 'L' dimensions are equal
Add rounded edge callouts to prevent sharp transitions at seal seat entries
Specify plunge grinding surface finish requirement on seal seat surfaces to eliminate helical grinding marks
Generate assembly sequence constraints: seal ring installation must follow bearing installation when diameters match
summary: This standard defines the geometry requirements for seal ring housing working zones, including mandatory 15° ± 5° lead-in chamfers with diameter-dependent fillet radii (0.4 to 1.2 mm) and effective working dimensions constrained between 1-2 mm. Special rules apply when bearing and seal ring share the same fitting diameter, requiring matched zone dimensions and specific assembly sequences. Surface finish must prevent sharp edges and helical ridges, preferably using plunge grinding.
